content:
After months of testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is officially rolling out to all users, bringing an all-new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, major new Safari features, and a host of performance and usability improvements. Here's everything you need to know about this update.

At this year's WWDC, Apple introduced its operating systems in a way that was slightly different from what users and developers were used to.

Rather than walking through each platform's new features individually, Apple spent less time on individual operating systems and focused on cross-platform features and improvements, largely because many of those features rely on the new Apple Intelligence framework.

That said, macOS 27 Golden Gate still includes a number of thoughtful design and feature improvements, starting with several much-needed Liquid Glass adjustments.

Liquid Glass and Interface Improvements

Although macOS Tahoe 26 adopted Apple's brand-new design language, it still lagged behind other systems visually—especially iOS 26 and iPadOS 26.

In macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has spent more time further integrating the new Liquid Glass into the system, while also bringing in some of the visual tweaks from iOS 27 and iPadOS 27—including a new Liquid Glass slider that lets users adjust the transparency of the effect themselves.

Hidden within the Liquid Glass appearance settings is a fun Easter egg featuring Clarus the Dogcow—just keep scrolling the demo panel past the bottom and you'll spot him.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also features refreshed app icons that better match the Liquid Glass design, with more layers adding depth and detail to global system settings like Light, Dark, Tinted, and Clear.

The traffic light buttons (red, yellow, green) that Apple introduced mid-way through beta testing have also been updated. The previous flat green, yellow, and red controls now sport a Liquid Glass look, and when users click (or tap, not too far from now?) and drag them before releasing, there's a delightful bounce effect.

Another thoughtful interface improvement in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Apple's decision to standardize window and app corner radii across the system, rather than dynamically adjusting them based on UI elements in the window's menu bar.

Although Apple's move was intentional, many assumed the inconsistent corner radii were a bug—prompting Apple to specifically call out the change during the WWDC keynote.

Another controversial design decision involved icon counts. macOS 26 Tahoe added a symbol next to nearly every menu command, ostensibly to make menus more scannable—but the result was widely criticized as making the interface more cluttered and harder to scan in some cases.

Fortunately, with macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has reversed course, removing most of those icons and returning menus to a cleaner, less ornate look.

Other visual refinements in macOS 27 Golden Gate include edge-to-edge sidebars and clearer delineation of the active window—both of which were points of contention in macOS Tahoe 26.

Siri AI and the New Siri App

This is arguably the biggest new feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate. The new Siri, developed in partnership with Google's Gemini models, gets its own dedicated app and is deeply integrated throughout the system.

The new Siri AI uses a new on-device indexing system to handle user data, and exists simultaneously within Spotlight and the new Siri app.

The new Siri app looks and works largely like other AI assistant apps: a sidebar listing the user's chat history across compatible platforms, with a main chat panel where you can enter prompts, attach images or files, or initiate a conversation by voice. The app also supports search and pinned conversations—a plus for users with different workflows.

The new Siri AI can draw from the web and the user's personal information to provide practical, actionable answers. During beta, the new Siri received overwhelmingly positive reviews, even though it can sometimes be slower than users accustomed to other LLM-powered AI assistants might expect.

Another practical feature of the new Siri AI is its ability to interact with both native and third-party apps and perform actions directly—vastly improving on the app integration capabilities of the old Siri.

Developers need to expose their apps' content and functionality through the App Intents framework, so as more developers update their apps for macOS 27 Golden Gate, this aspect is expected to continue improving.

Finally, the system gains a universal "Ask Siri" right-click menu option, allowing users to select text, images, or files and ask Siri directly. For example, you can Control-click an image in a document and ask Siri for more information, or select a passage of text and ask Siri to rewrite, proofread, adjust the tone, or provide writing suggestions.

Siri AI launches with English support, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish being added in October. Due to regulatory reasons, Siri AI is currently unavailable in China and the EU.

Apple Intelligence

We've already covered Apple's brand-new foundation models in detail, but in short, with its 2027 OS releases, Apple has developed a new generation of Apple Intelligence models. Here's Apple's official description of each model:

AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3-billion parameter dense model, with further quality improvements. AFM 3 Core Advanced, our most powerful on-device model, natively multimodal and supporting more expressive voice and higher-accuracy dictation. Built on Apple's most cutting-edge research, this 20-billion parameter model uses a sparse architecture, activating only 1 to 4 billion parameters at a time as needed. AFM 3 Core Advanced requires and is optimized for our most powerful Apple Silicon systems. AFM 3 Cloud, our server-side workhorse model, designed for speed, efficiency, and capability. ADM 3 Cloud (Image), used for image generation and editing, unlocking more advanced photo editing tools, the new Image Playground, and more. AFM 3 Cloud Pro, our most powerful server-side model, powering our most challenging use cases, such as agentic tool use and complex reasoning.

In practice, macOS 27 Golden Gate uses two on-device models—AFM 3 Core and AFM 3 Core Advanced—with the remaining models based in the cloud. The performance of these two on-device models depends on the Mac's hardware, particularly available memory, to handle their active parameters and other AI workloads.

When it comes to Apple Intelligence's real-world performance in macOS 27 Golden Gate, it's a mixed bag. The models themselves perform quite well on everyday tasks—such as helping draft emails, proofreading documents, or summarizing content.

The problem is that Apple now seems to be somewhat overzealous about how and when it surfaces Siri AI—sometimes overwhelming users and even getting in the way of what they're trying to accomplish.

One standout new Apple Intelligence feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new Visual Intelligence shortcut. Simply press Command-Shift-Space, and you can select any area of the screen and immediately ask Siri about it—whether it's an image, PDF, text, or virtually anything displayed on screen.

Unfortunately, not all Macs compatible with macOS 27 can run the new Apple Intelligence—features require an A18 Pro, M1, or later chip. Here's Apple's official list of Mac models that support the new features:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)
  • MacBook Air with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • MacBook Pro with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • iMac with Apple Silicon (2021 or later)
  • Mac mini with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • Mac Studio (2022 or later)
  • Mac Pro with Apple Silicon (2023)

Most Apple Intelligence features support the languages already available for Apple Intelligence, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Due to regulatory reasons, Apple Intelligence is currently unavailable in China. Apple has also stated that some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features will have usage limits, but the company has not yet released specific details.

Performance and Stability Improvements

In the WWDC26 keynote, Apple highlighted dozens of improvements that would apply across all its operating systems.

For macOS 27 Golden Gate, these include faster AirDrop transfers, improved network file browsing, faster Spotlight indexing (especially for shortcuts and actions), and faster iCloud Photos uploads with selective priority sync.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also improves scrolling performance in Safari and Calendar, as well as animation in Mission Control and Spaces. Apple has also tweaked Mail indexing and search, along with the underlying system for Spotlight suggestions.

Other refinements include more consistent and persistent window position memory across external displays, HDR support for system UI elements, broader support for high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes on external displays, and more complete touch support in Sidecar—including tap control, single-finger scrolling, system gestures, and Markup.

Safari

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a new Safari feature called "Notify Me," which can monitor web pages and alert users when relevant changes occur—such as price drops, restocks, event registration openings, or virtually anything else a user wants to track.

Notify Me can check hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly, and can additionally specify the days and times to perform checks.

Additionally, Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate gains "Describe an Extension," which lets users create extensions using natural language.

To help users get started, Apple provides several examples covering productivity, focus, creativity, and design and development. Users can also simply describe what they need in their own words, and leave the rest to Apple Intelligence.

Both features are accessible from the "More Options" hamburger menu on the right side of the current tab.

For users who love opening a mountain of tabs as the day unfolds, Safari can now automatically organize and group tabs by topic.

Another interesting detail in Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new pull-to-refresh gesture, similar to iOS and iPadOS, where users can swipe down past the "rubber band" effect to refresh the page.

This gesture also works in other system apps such as Mail, News, and Calendar; many see this move as further foreshadowing the rumored touch-enabled Mac, which could be announced as early as this year.

iPhone Mirroring

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, users can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window to different aspect ratios; many see this as an early sign that Apple is paving the way for a foldable iPhone.

Now that iPhone Duo has officially launched, Mac users can get an early taste of this experience. Unfortunately, Apple notes that iPhone Mirroring is still unavailable in the EU.

Shortcuts

This could be one of the most practical new Apple Intelligence features in this year's OS updates.

Although Shortcuts itself is a relatively accessible automation tool, it can still feel daunting for everyday users. Now, users can simply describe what they want to accomplish, and Apple Intelligence will build it into a native shortcut.

To help users get started, the Shortcuts app will also highlight several suggestions on the new shortcut creation screen, including:

  • Dictate and translate to Spanish
  • Write a haiku about the weather forecast
  • Play my workout playlist when I arrive at the gym
  • Create a recipe from these leftovers
  • Summarize my day each morning
  • Prioritize my to-do list each morning
  • Get driving directions as soon as I get in the car
  • Dictate my thoughts and save them to the clipboard
  • Dim the screen when bedtime begins
  • Turn on Do Not Disturb when opening the TV app

By the way, if you want to dive deeper into Shortcuts, be sure to follow Stephen Robles on YouTube and Instagram. You can also check out Shortcuts Playground from MacStories, a more powerful natural language shortcut builder.

Photos

The Photos app now offers three Apple Intelligence-powered editing tools: an enhanced Clean Up that can remove objects, people, or other unwanted elements from photos; Extend, which can generate surrounding areas when you feel an original photo was cropped too tightly; and Spatial Reframing, which lets you change the angle and composition of a photo after it's been taken.

Additionally, iCloud Shared Albums now supports full-resolution sharing and can invite Windows and Android users to join via iCloud.com.

Other new features include the ability to play any set of photos and videos as a slideshow with custom music, transitions, and playback duration, a photo rating feature with a new star-based system, and a brand-new "Shot by Me" dedicated collection.

More macOS 27 Golden Gate Details

  • Calendar lets users add, edit, or update events by describing them.
  • Finder can now intelligently suggest names for files and folders based on their contents.
  • Image Playground has expanded support for different styles and uses a brand-new foundation model for better results.
  • Maps has an enhanced Flyover experience, with improved textures, detail, and clarity for hundreds of cities worldwide.
  • Messages has finally (finally) integrated tapback notifications and improved cross-device sync performance.
  • Notes supports handwriting and drawing with the trackpad, expanded Markdown support, and adds copy/paste and Section Links functionality.
  • Podcasts now supports video podcasts with picture-in-picture playback.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also marks the final version to support Rosetta. As Apple explains, "only apps will be unable to run on Macs with Apple Silicon after installing this update"—you can read more about it here.

Compatibility

According to Apple's official list, macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with the following Mac models:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)

Which new feature is your favorite? Let us know in the comments.
